info.title: Statwarden API
info.summary: Uptime monitoring, alerting and status pages.
info.description:
The `/api/v1` REST surface of an Statwarden instance, plus the operational endpoints a reverse proxy and a scraper depend on.

**Authentication.** Two principals are accepted. A browser session sends the `statwarden_session` cookie; every mutating request must additionally echo the readable `statwarden_csrf` cookie in the `X-CSRF-Token` header. A programmatic client sends `Authorization: Bearer <api key secret>` and is *exempt* from CSRF — a bearer client has no ambient cookie to be confused with.

**Authorization.** Endpoints state their requirement in the operation description as one of *any authenticated principal*, *writer* (role `user` or `admin`, plus the `write` scope for API keys) or *admin* (role `admin`, plus the `admin` scope). Endpoints marked *public* need no credential at all and are rate limited per client IP.

**Errors.** Every error is RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`. List endpoints return `{items,total,limit,offset}`.

**Try it out.** Requests issued from this page hit the live instance with your real session. There is no sandbox.

get.description: Admin. Streams audit entries newest first for the window given by `from`/`to`, capped at 50000 rows. When the window did not fit, the response carries `X-Statwarden-Export-Truncated: true` and the caller should narrow it — a CSV body has no way to say that it is incomplete. The export is itself recorded in the audit log as `audit.export`.

X-Statwarden-Export-Truncated.description: Present and "true" when the window exceeded the row cap and the body is partial.

post.description: Public, rate limited per IP and locked out per account after repeated failures. When 2FA is enabled the TOTP code (or a backup code) is verified in this same request — there is no separate challenge endpoint.

get.description: Public and rate-limited. Returns only the local id and display name - never the client id or secret. Registered only when single sign-on is configured; an instance without it serves no /auth/oidc route at all.

Public and rate-limited; the identity provider redirects the browser here. This is the URI that must be whitelisted at the provider, as {PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/api/v1/auth/oidc/{provider}/callback. It serves both the anonymous login mode and the authenticated link mode. An account is resolved by (issuer, subject) and NEVER by the asserted e-mail address; an unknown subject is refused unless auto-provisioning has been explicitly enabled. Always answers with a redirect - coarse `?error=` codes on failure, never problem+json. Registered only when single sign-on is configured; an instance without it serves no /auth/oidc route at all.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: The local provider id from GET /auth/oidc/providers.

302.description: Redirect to the dashboard on success, or to /login?error=... on failure.

get.description: Public and rate-limited. Redirects the browser to the identity provider with PKCE (S256), a state value and a nonce, all held in a short-lived HttpOnly cookie. Navigate to this URL in the address bar; it is not a fetch endpoint. Registered only when single sign-on is configured; an instance without it serves no /auth/oidc route at all.

parameters.name: provider

302.description: Redirect to the identity provider, or back to /login?error=... when the provider cannot be reached.

post.description: Public and rate-limited. The response is IDENTICAL for every outcome - address known, address unknown, account deactivated, mail not configured - so this endpoint cannot be used to discover whether an account exists. Do not build a client that treats the response as confirmation that an address is registered.

202.description: Accepted. Says nothing about whether an account exists.

post.description: Public and rate-limited. The token is single-use and expires after an hour. Every token failure - unknown, expired, already redeemed - returns the same 400, so a caller cannot learn that a token once existed. On success EVERY session of the account is revoked and the caller is NOT signed in: they must log in with the new password.

204.description: The password was changed and all sessions were revoked.

post.description: Any authenticated principal, including a viewer - a user owns their own profile; CSRF required. The subject is always the caller: there is no id parameter, so the endpoint cannot be pointed at another user. The image type is decided by sniffing the uploaded bytes, never by the declared Content-Type or the file name; PNG, JPEG and WebP are accepted and SVG is not. Maximum 1 MiB and 1024x1024 pixels.

415.description: Not a PNG, JPEG or WebP image.

delete.description: Any authenticated principal; CSRF required. Idempotent: a user without an avatar also gets 204.

put.description: Any authenticated principal; CSRF required. The current password must be supplied and is verified first: the address is where password-reset tokens are mailed, so a hijacked session must not be able to repoint it. 403 when the password is wrong; 409 when the account signs in through SSO and has no local password to check.

get.summary: List the caller's linked single-sign-on accounts
get.description: Any authenticated principal. Registered only when single sign-on is configured; an instance without it serves no /auth/oidc route at all.

delete.summary: Unlink one of the caller's single-sign-on accounts
delete.description: Any authenticated principal; CSRF required. Scoped to the caller's own links. Refuses with 409 when it would remove the last identity of an account that has no local password, which would otherwise be an irrecoverable self-lockout. Registered only when single sign-on is configured; an instance without it serves no /auth/oidc route at all.

post.summary: Begin linking a single-sign-on account to the caller
post.description: Any authenticated principal; CSRF required. A POST returning the authorize URL rather than a redirect, because linking is a mutation and a top-level GET navigation cannot carry the CSRF header. The resulting identity is attached to the CALLER, whatever the provider asserts about the address. Registered only when single sign-on is configured; an instance without it serves no /auth/oidc route at all.

get.description: Writer. Monitors deleted but not yet purged, most recently deleted first. Deleting a monitor is a soft delete: its heartbeats, tags, channel links and status-page placements are kept, and every other endpoint stops seeing it. Entries are removed for good after TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS, or immediately via the purge endpoint.

get.summary: List state transitions across all monitors
get.description: Every live monitor's important heartbeats (status changes), newest first, paged. Soft-deleted monitors are excluded. The dashboard home's event log; the per-monitor equivalent is /monitors/{id}/heartbeats?important=true.
Any authenticated principal.

put.description: Writer. CSRF required. This is a full replacement, not a patch.

delete.description: Writer. CSRF required. A SOFT delete: the monitor moves to the recycle bin with its heartbeats and associations intact, stops being checked, and disappears from every other read. GET /monitors/trash lists it, POST /monitors/{id}/restore brings it back (paused), and DELETE /monitors/{id}/purge destroys it for good. The bin is also emptied automatically once an entry has been in it longer than TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS.

post.summary: Restore a monitor from the recycle bin
post.description: Writer. CSRF required. The monitor comes back PAUSED: the store cannot know whether it was active before the delete, and resuming checks — and alerts — for something that has been gone for days is not what a restore should do on its own. 404 for a monitor that is not in the bin.

delete.description: Admin. CSRF required. Hard-deletes a monitor that is ALREADY in the recycle bin, taking its entire heartbeat history with it. This cannot be undone. It answers 404 for a live monitor: the only route to an irreversible delete runs through the bin, so there is always a window in which a mistake can be reversed. Admin-only for the same reason.

post.description: Writer. CSRF required. Asks the engine to probe now, out of schedule.

get.description: Public. Returns this OpenAPI description. It contains no instance data — only the shape of the API — which is why it needs no credential.

Public. Returns an HTML page that renders this document in the browser and can issue requests against the live instance. It fetches `/api/v1/openapi.json` at runtime and embeds no copy of the API surface, so it cannot drift from the spec. Served from the binary with no external assets, so it works offline and air-gapped.

Intended for a browser. A programmatic client wants the JSON document instead.

get.description: Public and rate limited. Resolves the page from the request Host header (custom-domain routing).
Public and rate limited. A password-protected page requires the page password.

parameters.description: Page access password, when the page is protected.

get.summary: Overall badge for a status page
get.description: Public and rate limited.

get.summary: Availability archive for a status page
get.description: Public and rate limited. Month-by-month availability over `months` calendar months (default 24, capped at 120); an out-of-range value is clamped rather than rejected, because a stray link must not become an error screen for a visitor. Monitors the page marks `show_uptime: false` are omitted entirely. A password-protected page requires the same password as the page itself.

parameters.name: months
parameters.description: Calendar months to include, newest last. Never rejected: above 120 is clamped to 120, and below 1 (or unparseable) falls back to the default of 24 rather than answering 400. This is a zoom level on a public page, and a stray link must not become an error screen for a visitor who cannot fix it — which is also why the schema states no minimum: one would promise a rejection that never happens.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Page access password, when the page is protected.

put.summary: Write or publish an incident postmortem
put.description: Writer. CSRF required. Replaces only the retrospective and its publication state; every other field of the incident is untouched, so a concurrent edit cannot be clobbered. Publishing requires a non-empty body and an incident whose status is `resolved` (409 otherwise). Re-publishing keeps the original publication timestamp.

patch.description: Writer. CSRF required. The payload must be a COMPLETE ordering: every group and every monitor currently on the page, each named exactly once. A partial ordering is rejected, which doubles as an optimistic concurrency check.

Public. Answers as soon as the process is serving; it does not touch the database.
Present only when metrics are enabled. May be gated behind a bearer token, in which case an unauthenticated scrape is refused. The endpoint is registered for all HTTP methods; only GET is meaningful.

200.description: Metrics in Prometheus text exposition format.

401.description: A metrics token is configured and was not supplied.

get.description: Public. Pings the database with a short timeout. Reports 503 when no pool is configured or the database is unreachable.

Unauthenticated, like the logo route. The file name is server-minted and carries 128 bits of entropy, and that unguessability is the only access control: anyone holding the URL can fetch the image, and the immutable caching means a proxy may retain it after deletion. Served with nosniff, a restrictive Content-Security-Policy and inline disposition.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The server-generated file name, as returned by the upload endpoint.

get.description: Public: logos are rendered by anonymous visitors of a public status page. The file name is server-minted and unguessable; anything not matching that shape is a 404. Served with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a restrictive `Content-Security-Policy` and immutable caching.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The server-generated file name, as returned by the upload endpoint.

sessionCookie.name: statwarden_session
sessionCookie.description: Browser session cookie, issued by `POST /api/v1/auth/login`. HttpOnly. Every mutating request must ALSO send the `X-CSRF-Token` header carrying the value of the readable `statwarden_csrf` cookie.

apiKey.description: An API key secret, as returned once by `POST /api/v1/me/api-keys`. Bearer principals are exempt from CSRF — do not send `X-CSRF-Token` with one. The key's scopes (`read`, `write`, `admin`) are checked in addition to the owning user's role.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 50, capped at 200. A non-positive or unparseable value falls back to the default.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: Number of items to skip. Defaults to 0.

BadgeToken.name: token
BadgeToken.description: The monitor's opaque badge token, minted via `POST /api/v1/monitors/{id}/badge`.

BadRequest.description: The request body or a parameter is invalid. Unknown JSON fields are rejected outright.

Unauthorized.description: No valid session or API key was presented.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but the role or API-key scope is insufficient — or the CSRF header is missing or does not match the cookie.

Conflict.description: The resource already exists, or the state transition is not allowed.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests from this client IP.

Unavailable.description: The optional subsystem backing this endpoint is not configured in this deployment.

APIKey.description: A scoped programmatic credential. The secret is never in this object.

prefix.description: The leading, non-secret part of the key, for identifying it in a list.

expires_in_days.description: The key's lifetime in whole days from now. Omit the field for a key that never expires; 0 is rejected, so that "no expiry" cannot be requested by accident. The resulting instant is returned as expires_at, and the key is refused from that moment on.

totp_code.description: A current authenticator code, or one of the caller's backup codes. Required when the account has two-factor authentication enabled; a backup code is consumed when it is the one that matched.

secret.description: The bearer secret. Shown here and never again.

days_remaining.description: Whole days until expiry. NEGATIVE once the certificate has lapsed.

AuthResult.description: The signed-in user plus the CSRF token to echo on subsequent mutations. The session itself lives in the `statwarden_session` cookie.

backup_codes.description: Single-use recovery codes, returned in plaintext exactly once. The server stores only their hashes.

action.description: The action to apply to every listed monitor.

tag_ids.description: Required by the `tag` action, ignored otherwise.

group_id.description: Used by the `group` action; null clears the folder.

error.description: Short client-facing reason; empty when OK.

current_password.description: The caller's current password. The e-mail address is the account recovery channel, so changing it is re-authenticated exactly like a password change.

ExternalIdentity.description: A link between a local account and an account at an identity provider. The join key is (issuer, subject); the e-mail address is display-only and is never used to resolve an account.

important.description: True when this heartbeat changed the monitor's status.

postmortem.description: Retrospective written after the incident closed (Markdown). Absent on the public status page unless postmortem_published_at is set.

postmortem_published_at.description: When the retrospective was published. ABSENT — not null — while it is still a draft: the field is omitempty, so a draft carries no key at all.

body.description: The retrospective, Markdown. Empty clears it.

published.description: Publish to the public status page. Requires a non-empty body and a resolved incident.

LayoutReorderRequest.description: A COMPLETE re-statement of a page's display order. Every group and every monitor currently on the page must appear exactly once.

ListEnvelope.description: The paginated list shape shared by every list endpoint that pages.

total.description: Total matching rows, ignoring the page window.

totp_code.description: Required when the account has 2FA enabled.

backup_code.description: A single-use backup code, accepted in place of `totp_code`.

strategy.description: How the window recurs; `single` is a one-off.

timezone.description: IANA zone the window is evaluated in.

Monitor.description: The read shape of a monitor: a superset of MonitorInput plus derived state.

config.description: Type-specific configuration, validated by that type's checker.

recovery_checks.description: Consecutive successful checks a DOWN monitor needs before it counts as UP again.

upside_down.description: Inverts the verdict: a reachable target counts as down.

status.description: Current status: pending, up, down, paused or maintenance.

url.description: Read-only display target lifted out of `config`. Ignored on write.

recent_beats.description: Status of the newest heartbeats (at most 50), oldest first: the per-check bar of the monitor list. Unlike sparkline it keeps beats without a latency, so a DOWN check is never dropped.

scheduling_error.description: Present only when the write succeeded but the scheduler refused the monitor: the row is active and nothing is checking it. Absent on every normal response. Returned by POST /monitors and PUT /monitors/{id}, which still answer 201/200 because the resource does exist — a 5xx there would invite a retry that creates a duplicate.

MonitorInput.description: The write shape of a monitor. Unknown fields are rejected.

config.description: Type-specific configuration. Defaults to `{}` when omitted.

recovery_checks.description: Consecutive successful checks a DOWN monitor needs before it counts as UP again. Omitted or 0 means 1.

passive.description: True for push-style types, which are not probed on a schedule.

config.description: Provider configuration. Secret fields are redacted on read and sealed at rest.

OIDCProviderInfo.description: A configured identity provider, as advertised to the login page. Carries no client credentials.

PasswordResetAccepted.description: The single response the request endpoint ever returns, whatever the outcome.

token.description: The opaque token from the mailed link.

type.description: Always `about:blank`; the status code carries the meaning.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation. Absent on the router's own 404/405.

Session.description: A server-side session. `id` is a fingerprint, never the cookie token.

logo_path.description: Server-owned. Written only by the logo endpoints; a client PUT cannot set it.

accent_color.description: Lowercase `#rrggbb`, or empty for the product accent.

has_password.description: Derived. The hash itself never leaves the server.

monitor_ids.description: Flat, in display order. Kept for backward compatibility alongside `groups`/`monitors`.

logo_path.description: Accepted and ignored; the logo is owned by the upload endpoints.

password.description: Plaintext page access password; hashed on save. Omit to leave unchanged.

group_name.description: Groups are matched or created by name on save.

StepUpConfirmation.description: Re-authentication. Required by the operations that change how an account can be signed into — minting an API key, enrolling an authenticator, linking a single-sign-on account, reissuing backup codes — because a session cookie alone would let a borrowed session turn itself into access that outlives the session and survives a password change. An account provisioned through single sign-on has no local password and no second factor to re-prove; for it the check is skipped and audited.

totp_code.description: A current authenticator code, or one of the caller's backup codes. Required when the account has two-factor authentication enabled; a backup code is consumed when it is the one that matched.

PublicUptimeBar.description: One uptime bucket. `uptime` is a 0..1 fraction, or -1 when the bucket holds no conclusive heartbeat.

start.description: Bucket boundary, UTC. The unambiguous key at any granularity.

date.description: The bucket's UTC day, kept for the legacy heatmap.

PublicHistory.description: Availability archive: one uptime bucket per calendar month per monitor, oldest first. `overall` and each monitor's `months` are parallel to `months`.

overall.description: Page-wide availability per month: the mean over the monitors with data that month, or -1 when none have any.
